primary_source_description: 1 medium onion, chopped 2 tbsp vegetable oil 1 (19 oz.) can enchilada sauce 1 (16 oz) can black beans, rinsed and drained 1 (14 1/2-oz) can diced tomatoes with jalapenos 1 (11 oz.) can Mexican-style corn, drained 1 tsp fajita seasoning or chili powder 1 tsp ground cumin 1 (10 oz.) pkg 6-inch corn tortillas (I used flour instead - it was fine) 3 cups chopped cook chicken (I used a cooked rotisserie chicken from the store and picked it from the bone) 3 cups (12 oz.) shredded Mexican four-cheese blend Saute onion in hot oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until tender. Stir in next 6 ingredients. Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring often, 5 min. or until thoroughly heated. Spoon one-third of the sauce mixture into a lightly greased 13x9-inch baking dish. Layer with one-third of tortillas, half of chopped chicken, and 1 cup cheese. Repeat layers with one-third each of sauce mixture and tortillas, remaining chicken and 1 cup cheese. Top with remaining tortillas, sauce mixture and 1 cup cheese. Bake at 350 degrees for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden and bubbly. (You may also substitute 2 lbs lean ground beef, cooked, for the chicken, if desired.) [ via Southern Living's 2002 Annual Recipes ]

primary_source_description: A friend got this very generic recipe off of Pinterest, but the pin was linked to a completely random and unrelated page, so I'm not sure where the original came from. The recipe in its original form: No-Bake Energy Bites 1 cup (dry) oatmeal 1/2 cup chocolate chips 1/2 cup peanut butter 1/2 cup ground flaxseed 1/3 cup honey 1 tsp. vanilla How I made them: 1 cup (dry) oatmeal 1 scoop vanilla protein powder 1/2 cup raisins 1/2 cup peanut butter 1/2 cup whole flaxseed* 1/3 cup honey *Note: I should have used ground flaxseed but I am a dope and got the whole seeds. They are still tasty, they just have a slightly odd crunch to them. You just mix everything together and then split them into whatever portions you want and roll them into balls! Mine are .7oz which makes 24 and puts them at an even 90 calories. You can split them however you see fit based on what you put in them! The friend I got this from took the original recipe and removed the vanilla and flaxseed, then just added a scoop of vanilla protein powder. So, as you can see these are very customizable! This is a great recipe that you can play around with and add whatever nutrition to that you want (i.e. flaxseed for the omega-3 and/or protein powder, etc). If you stick with the basics of oatmeal, peanut butter, and honey you will likely always end up with something sweet and cookie like to eat that's much healthier for you!

primary_source_description: Hab ich geliebt, als ich klein war! :) "Geschweldi" sind einfach nur Pellkartoffeln. "Bibiliskäs" ist ein Schwarzwälder Frischkäse. Wahrscheinlich die einzige echte Käsespezalität des Schwarzwalds. Ist seltsam, weil der Schwarzwald eigentlich Weideland mit Milchvieh-Wirtschaft ist. In anderen alemannischen Gegegenden mit Weidewirtschaft wie der Schweiz, dem französischen Elsass oder Algäu gibt es viele Käsesorten. Auch rhein-abwärts, in den Niederlanden.... Im Schwarzwald isst man den Käse aber komischerweise frisch. Und selbst.... ;) "Bibiliskäs" Ist entfernt ein bisschen vergleichbar mit griechischem Tzaziki... "Bibili"ist alemannisch für Küken = junges Huhn. Also ein junger Frischkäse. Kann alemannisch auch "Biberli" bedeuten = kleine Klümpchen. Schwarzwälder Bibiliskäs ist schwer zu bekommen. Selbst wenn man am Rande des Schwarzwalds lebt . Man kann allerdings auch Quark mit etwas Sahne und Salz verwenden. Kommt dem Bibiliskäs nahe. So kenn ich's. Frisch gekochte Pellkartoffeln sind was tolles. Hab immer Pellkartoffeln gegessen, wenn meine Mutter frische Kartoffeln für badischen Kartoffelsalat gekocht hat. Warme, frische Pellkartoffeln einfach nur mit Butter und Salz!!! ....oder eben mit Bibiliskäs :-)
